docRequirement: settings.md:633-651 (§ "Compute managed settings with a policy helper") binds us to a `policyHelper` setting, honored ONLY from MDM or a system `managed-settings.json` and ignored in every other scope including server-managed settings, that carries `path` (absolute path to the helper executable), `timeoutMs` (how long to wait before treating the run as failed) and `refreshIntervalMs` (re-run interval; `0` disables refresh, otherwise at least `60000`). The helper writes a JSON envelope to stdout whose settings sit under a `managedSettings` key; when it emits `managedSettings`, "that object becomes the only managed settings source for the run, taking precedence over remote, MDM, and file-based sources", and "When the helper exits non-zero at startup, Claude Code prints the error and refuses to start". settings.md:665 puts `policyHelper` output at the top of the managed tier, and :670 says that while a helper is configured its output is the only source the cross-source exception keys are read from.
current: The mechanism does not exist in any form. `policyHelper` appears exactly once in shipped source — `packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:29`, inside a docblock quoting Claude's managed-tier precedence chain ("`policyHelper` > remote > MDM > file-based > HKCU"); a binary-safe `grep -rna --binary-files=text "policyHelper" packages apps scripts` returns that line plus only generated bundles under `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/`. It is not a key: `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501-534`) lists 33 keys and none is `policyHelper`, so `refuseUnknownKeys` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:727-733`) drops it with `invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper` at disposition `stripped`, printed by `reportManagedPolicyDrops` (`packages/shared/src/config/managed-drops.ts:183-192`) from `createStorageRuntime` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:247`). It is not a source: `EnforcedManagedPolicySeams` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:53-58`) declares exactly two seams, `file` and `delivered`, and `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127-139`) composes only those two through `composeManagedPolicySources` (`packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:184-214`), whose winner enum `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1` (`packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:130`) is `'delivered' | 'file' | 'none'`. Nothing spawns a policy executable: `grep -rna --binary-files=text -e spawnSync -e execFileSync packages/shared/src/config packages/server-core/src/bootstrap packages/server-core/src/pi-harness` hits only test files and `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:2` (process teardown). No refresh timer exists for a helper — the only managed poll is the delivery poll `MANAGED_DELIVERY_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (`packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:74`). The eligible scope the doc names DOES exist in this fork: `managedPiPolicyPathForPlatform` (`packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52`) resolves `/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json` and `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json`, read under a host-owned regime (`safeNode` :74-76, `assertPosixOwnerAndMode` :78-81). A startup-refusal path also already exists and is wired to both hosts: `ManagedSettingsStartupError` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:72`), `assertManagedVersionAllowed` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:117-133`), applied at `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645-654` and `apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1101-1111` (dialog + `app.exit(1)`), and both sites deliberately read the host-owned FILE only — the same scope restriction the doc puts on `policyHelper`. The only helper-executable identifier anywhere near this is `headersHelper`, and it belongs to the MCP subsystem, is read-and-reported-not-implemented (`packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:1047-1055`, `packages/shared/src/mcp/project-config.ts:137-147`), and is not this.
divergence: The whole mechanism is absent — this is not a key-name or value mismatch that a rename would fix. Four separable pieces are missing: (1) `policyHelper` is not a recognised managed key, so the admin-authored value is stripped rather than read; (2) nothing spawns the executable at `path` with `timeoutMs`, so no `managedSettings` envelope is ever parsed; (3) the managed tier has no helper seam, so even a parsed helper output could not become the single winning source ahead of `delivered` and `file`; (4) there is no `refreshIntervalMs` re-run timer and no non-zero-exit startup refusal for it. The precedence RULE we do implement is correct for the two sources we have — winner-takes-all, no merge (`packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:184-214`) — so the delta is the missing top rung of that ordering, not a wrong ordering. Scope note on the recorded justification: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-server-managed-delivery.md:212-215` puts `policyHelper` out of scope as "OS-policy sources only", which correctly excludes it from the server-DELIVERED channel (settings.md:633 agrees it is ignored there) but says nothing about the system-FILE scope, which the same sentence names as valid and which this fork ships. The audit row is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:193` (R25b, "Record as C" = documented, not implemented) — an open item, not a closed owner decision.

change.what: Add a `policyHelper?: ManagedPolicyHelperV1` field to `ManagedPiPolicyV1` and the string `'policyHelper'` to `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` (:501-534) — without the key, `refuseUnknownKeys` (:727) strips it before anything downstream can see it. Add a `parsePolicyHelper` branch in `parsePolicy` under the tolerant sink: `path` a required absolute string (reject relative, reject `~`), `timeoutMs` an optional positive finite number with a bounded default, `refreshIntervalMs` an optional number that is either exactly `0` or `>= 60000` per the doc's table — any defect drops the WHOLE `policyHelper` object as `stripped` (never a partial helper config), matching the tolerant posture the file's docblock at :1487-1497 states. Do NOT add it to `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_WIDENING_KEYS`: helper output replaces the tier rather than widening a key, so `isManagedPolicyTightening` (:625-640) must not see a helper-sourced policy as a plain key delta — gate the re-read on source identity instead (see managed-policy-resolution below). The docblock at :495-500 states that a new field must also be pinned in the deliverability tests; honour it.

New module. `runManagedPolicyHelper(helper: ManagedPolicyHelperV1, deps): { policy, drops }`. Steps: (a) validate `helper.path` under the SAME host-owned regime the policy file uses — no symlink, `isFile()`, on POSIX `uid === 0` and `(mode & 0o022) === 0`; `safeNode` and `assertPosixOwnerAndMode` are currently module-private at `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/managed-policy-loader.ts:74-81`, so export them or lift both into a shared `managed-host-ownership.ts` — a user-writable helper binary named by a root-owned policy file is arbitrary code execution at every startup; (b) `execFileSync(path, [], { timeout: timeoutMs, encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: MAX_MANAGED_POLICY_BYTES })` reusing the 262144-byte cap at `managed-policy-loader.ts:20`; (c) non-zero exit, spawn failure or timeout throws a refusal carrying the first line of stderr plus recovery text — do not fall back to the file policy, the doc says refuse to start; (d) `JSON.parse` stdout, require a plain object, read the `managedSettings` property ONLY (a bare settings object at the top level must apply nothing, per the doc's explicit warning), and parse that through `parseManagedPiPolicyTolerantV1` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:1498-1505`) with `source: '<helper path>'`; (e) strip a nested `policyHelper` out of the helper's own output so a helper cannot chain into another helper. The envelope's sibling keys `claudeMd` and `appendSystemPrompt` have no counterpart in `ManagedPiPolicyV1` (grep for `appendSystemPrompt` under `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness` and `packages/shared/src/config` returns nothing) — record them as ignored-with-a-drop rather than silently discarding.

Add a third seam `helper?: (config) => ManagedPiPolicyLoadV1` to `EnforcedManagedPolicySeams` (:53-58). In `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy` (:127-139), load `file` first (it is the only scope allowed to carry the key), and when `file.policy.policyHelper !== undefined`, run the helper and return its output as the SOLE source — bypassing `composeManagedPolicySources` entirely, including the cross-source lock composition, because settings.md:670 says the helper's output is the only source those exception keys are read from. Return `winner: 'helper'` and keep `fileCarriesSettings` computed as today so the shadow warning can fire. Never read `policyHelper` off `delivered`.

Extend the union at :130 with `'helper'` and extend the module docblock (:12-35) so the recorded precedence chain and the implemented one agree — today :29 quotes a chain we do not implement. `composeManagedPolicySources` itself needs no change: the helper path bypasses it.

Add a `helper` row to `WINNER_LABEL` (:231-235), e.g. `'Managed settings (policy helper)'`, and print the helper path in `buildConfigDoctorReport`'s source section (:426-444) the way `file`/`delivered` already are. `shadowedManagedFileWarning` (:253-264) currently returns early unless `winner === 'delivered'`; it must also fire for `'helper'`, because a helper win shadows a file policy exactly the same way and that state is likewise invisible from disk.

No structural change at :234 — `resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy()` already returns the composed policy and the winner — but the helper refusal must be raised BEFORE this call so the app never boots on a stale policy. Add a `assertManagedPolicyHelperSucceeded()`-style call beside the existing version gate at `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645-654` and `apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1101-1111`, reusing `ManagedSettingsStartupError` (`headless-start.ts:72`) so both hosts' existing handlers (stderr + non-zero exit; `dialog.showErrorBox` + `app.exit(1)`) apply unchanged.

Install the `refreshIntervalMs` timer alongside `startManagedDeliveryPolling` (~:167-172) and return its teardown in the same closure. On each tick re-run the helper and republish; a MID-RUN non-zero exit must NOT kill the process (the doc scopes refusal to startup) — log and keep the previous policy. The consumer already exists: `SessionManager.refreshManagedPiPolicy` (`packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3477-3500`) fails safe on a throwing seam and holds a non-tightening change to the next turn boundary, reached through `resolveManagedPiPolicy` / `subscribeManagedPolicyChange` (`packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:455-456`). `subscribeManagedPolicyChange` currently only forwards `onManagedDeliveryChange`; it must also fire on a helper refresh.

Explicitly strip `policyHelper` from a DELIVERED payload with a recorded drop (`MANAGED_DELIVERY_SOURCE`, :187). Once the key is in `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` it would otherwise parse and be cached to `managed-delivery.json` (:79, mode 0600), which the doc forbids — a gateway-delivered helper path is remote code execution at startup. This is the single highest-risk line of the whole change.

Positive: an envelope under `managedSettings` becomes the enforced policy and beats both a file policy and a delivered payload. Negatives: bare top-level settings object applies nothing; non-zero exit throws `ManagedSettingsStartupError`; timeout throws; a non-root-owned or group-writable helper path is refused; `refreshIntervalMs` of `30000` is dropped while `0` and `60000` are accepted; a delivered payload carrying `policyHelper` records a drop and spawns nothing. Extend `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-delivered-policy.test.ts` for helper-beats-delivered and `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.test.ts` for the key round-trip the :495-500 docblock demands.

blastRadius: Crosses BOTH a persistence and a wire boundary, so it is a risk trigger in this repo. Persistence: `policyHelper` becomes a key of the admin-authored managed-policy document (`/Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json`, `/etc/nessy/managed-policy.json`, `%ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json` — `managed-policy-loader.ts:44-52`) and of its `managed-policy.d/` fragments, which deep-merge (`mergeManagedPolicySources`, `managed-policy-loader.ts:180-198`). Wire: the same schema is the server-delivered payload, salvaged and cached at mode 0600 in `managed-delivery.json` (`packages/shared/src/config/managed-delivery.ts:79-157`); the key MUST be stripped on that path or a gateway response becomes startup code execution. Process lifecycle: a new `execFileSync` of an admin-named binary on every cold start, plus a background refresh timer. Startup refusal: `apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:1101-1111` and `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/headless-start.ts:645-654` — a wrong exit condition here refuses to start every managed install in the fleet. Direct readers to update: `MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS` has 6 consumers inside `managed-policy.ts` (`isManagedPolicyTightening` :629, `refuseUnknownKeys` :728, and the canonicalisation/equality helpers) and is pinned by `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/managed-policy-reread.test.ts`, `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.test.ts`, `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-delivered-policy.test.ts`, `packages/shared/src/marketplace/__tests__/delivered-marketplace-policy.test.ts`. `ManagedPolicyWinnerV1` readers: `config-doctor.ts:231/253/422`, `storage-runtime.ts:254-258`, `apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:42,80`. `EnforcedManagedPolicySeams` callers: `storage-runtime.ts:234,455`, `managed-policy-resolution.ts:162,281`, `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/config-doctor-input.test.ts:21,33,43`. Not touched: the imported-plugin adapters — `headersHelper` in `format-adapters/claude.ts:1047` and `mcp/project-config.ts:137` is a different subsystem and must stay read-and-reported.
userImpact: None observable for ordinary users — latent, and administrator-facing. Concretely today: an admin who follows Claude's page and deploys `{"policyHelper": {"path": "/usr/local/bin/nessy-policy", "refreshIntervalMs": 300000}}` in the system managed-policy file gets the key silently ignored as policy and loudly ignored as a diagnostic — `refuseUnknownKeys` records `invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper` (managed-policy.ts:731), `reportManagedPolicyDrops` prints `[managed-settings] …` to stderr/the main log at startup (managed-drops.ts:190 via storage-runtime.ts:247), and the same drop appears under `Invalid managed entries` in `nessy-general-agent doctor` (config-doctor.ts:446-451). The app then starts and enforces whatever the static file or the delivered payload says. Nothing crashes and nothing is mis-enforced, so an end user sees nothing at all; what the organisation loses is the ability to derive policy from device posture, identity or a remote service, and the ability to have a per-device policy refresh on an interval it chooses. It surfaces the moment an admin deploys the key and either reads the startup log or runs the doctor.
